name: 2012 VP113
axesStatus: Illustrative equal axes at the diameter its discoverers estimate for an assumed albedo of 0.10; not measured.
credit: Sheppard & Trujillo (2016), The Astronomical Journal 152, 221, Table 2: diameter 550 km for an assumed albedo of 0.10
shapeMeaning: Illustrative sphere 550 km across, the diameter Sheppard & Trujillo (2016, Table 2) estimate from its brightness for an assumed moderate albedo of 0.10. The size is not measured.
orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole, arbitrary prime meridian and phase; no spin pole is published.
surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed color or terrain.
introduction: 2012 VP113 never comes closer to the Sun than about 80 au, and at the far end of its orbit it is about 450 au away. Its discoverers reported it in 2014 as a second Sedna-like body.
card: A Sedna-like body that never comes closer than about 80 au.
datasetSummary: A sphere 550 km across, the size its discoverers estimate for an assumed albedo.
